nameStory: **Note: This appears to be a microscopic algae, not a plant typically found by nature explorers.** The scientific name Planktosphaeria gelatinosa literally means "gel-like floating sphere," which perfectly describes this tiny aquatic organism. The name comes from the Greek words for "wandering" (planktos), "sphere" (sphaeria), and "jelly-like" (gelatinosa).
description: **Uncertain identification - limited training data available.** Planktosphaeria gelatinosa appears to be a microscopic, single-celled algae that forms small, jelly-like spherical colonies in freshwater. These tiny organisms are invisible to the naked eye and would require a microscope to observe properly. With only 2 recorded observations in New England, this is an extremely rare find that most nature explorers would never encounter in typical field conditions.
